title: Contraction from self-adjointness
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set with weights $w_i\ge0$, and let $T$ be an operator from real-valued functions on $I$ to real-valued functions on $I$. Suppose that $\sum_{i\in I}w_i(Tf)_i g_i=\sum_{i\in I}w_i f_i(Tg)_i$ for all functions $f,g:I\to\mathbb R$. For $q>1$, suppose also that $\left(\sum_iw_i|(Tg)_i|^{q/(q-1)}\right)^{1/(q/(q-1))}\le\left(\sum_iw_i|g_i|^{q/(q-1)}\right)^{1/(q/(q-1))}$ for every $g:I\to\mathbb R$. Then $\left(\sum_iw_i|(Tf)_i|^q\right)^{1/q}\le\left(\sum_iw_i|f_i|^q\right)^{1/q}$ for every $f:I\to\mathbb R$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ maps real-valued functions on $I$ to real-valued functions on $I$
The weighted self-adjointness identity holds for all $f,g$
The stated weighted norm contraction holds for every $g$
replaced: Let $I$ be a finite set with nonnegative weights $w_i$ and define $\|f\|_{r,w}=(\sum_iw_i|f_i|^r)^{1/r}$. If an operator $T$ satisfies $\sum_iw_i(Tf)_ig_i=\sum_iw_if_i(Tg)_i$ for all $f,g$ and $\|Tg\|_{q/(q-1),w}\le\|g\|_{q/(q-1),w}$ for every $g$, where $q>1$, then $\|Tf\|_{q,w}\le\|f\|_{q,w}$ for every $f$.
